chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn Ḥadīd and Ibn Abī ʿUmayr together, from Jamīl ibn Darrāj, from a man, from one of the two عليهما السلام, concerning:

A man who stole, or drank wine, or committed zina, but that was not known from him and he was not apprehended until he repented and reformed—he said: “If he has reformed and something good is recognized from him, the hadd is not carried out upon him.”

Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr said: I said, “Even if it was something recent, the hadd is not carried out upon him?” He said: “Even if it was five months or less, and something good has appeared from him, the hudud are not carried out upon him.”

key_terms.أَمْرٌ جَمِيلٌ: good and commendable conduct that becomes evident
key_terms.شَرِبَ الْخَمْرَ: drank wine, meaning consumed an intoxicant unlawfully

ai.seo_question: Is the hadd punishment dropped if a person repents and reforms before being apprehended?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a person who committed theft, drank wine, or committed zina, but was not exposed or arrested before repenting and reforming. If genuine reform and good conduct become evident, the prescribed hadd punishment is not carried out upon him, even if the offense had occurred relatively recently.
